introduction: Maryland TDAP provides cash help to eligible low-income adults with disabilities who do not have dependent children. It can support a short disability period or a pending federal disability claim.

who: A licensed medical practitioner must complete the disability report. Financial and other eligibility conditions apply.
If disability is expected to last 12 months or longer, the applicant must apply for SSI. State assistance has time limits that differ when SSI is being pursued.
sections.get: Approved TDAP provides cash support. It is a state program with its own decision; it does not replace an SSI application or guarantee federal disability approval.
sections.docs: Ask the local department for the medical-report form and have the licensed practitioner complete it. Prepare income information and any SSI filing confirmation or correspondence.
sections.apply:
1. Apply at Maryland Benefits or the local Department of Social Services.
  2. Submit the required medical report and financial verification.
  3. If the expected disability lasts at least 12 months, file SSI as instructed and give the worker proof of the claim.
sections.after: Keep medical and SSI documents current and respond to the worker’s requests. The state generally limits TDAP to 12 months in a 36-month period unless the recipient is pursuing SSI. Ask how that rule applies to your case.

faqs: Yes. Maryland requires a report completed by a licensed medical practitioner.
Is this the family cash program?
No. TDAP is intended for eligible individuals without dependent children; TCA serves qualifying families.
Applicants disabled for 12 months or more must file an SSI application.
Can TDAP continue while SSI is pending?
The state describes an exception to the ordinary time limit for recipients pursuing SSI. Ask the worker what proof and continuing requirements apply.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
